audit.description: Changed production code in casanova/http.py imports aiohttp and uses real aiohttp APIs including TCPConnector, ClientSession, and session.get inside the request path. The urllib3 import and PoolManager/request usage were removed from the changed production file, and setup.py now declares aiohttp for the http extra instead of urllib3. Dynamic evidence records target imports from casanova/http.py resolving to site-packages/aiohttp with zero source import attempts and target_local_spec_count 0, so the target use is not a local fake provider.
evidence: Unified diff: casanova/http.py replaces import urllib3 with import aiohttp and changes urllib3_installed/pool_manager logic to aiohttp_installed plus aiohttp.TCPConnector and aiohttp.ClientSession
Unified diff: request(url) now returns asyncio.run(_request(url)); _request uses session.get(url) and await response.read()
Static anti-cheat: casanova/http.py imports_target=true, imports_source=false, fake_target_added_code=false, target_provider_added=false
Dynamic anti-cheat: first target_import from casanova/http.py line 12 resolves to after_venv_overlay/.../site-packages/aiohttp/__init__.py; source_import_attempt_count=0; target_local_spec_count=0
reasons: casanova/http.py meaningfully uses aiohttp APIs in production code
changed production code no longer imports or references urllib3
dynamic evidence shows aiohttp loaded from site-packages and no local target shim
